verdict.rationale: Grafana documents its own CI/CD automation path. Observability-as-code defines dashboards, data sources and other configuration in code for CI/CD pipelines, and a terminal CLI that authenticates and runs administrative tasks is described as suitable for CI/CD. File-based provisioning, an official CLI and an OpenAPI spec back this up. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of CI use, detailed docs on non-interactive CLI auth and command coverage.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: You can authenticate, manage multiple environments, and perform administrative tasks from the terminal. It’s suitable for CI/CD pipelines, local development
This approach lets you define dashboards, data sources, and other configurations in code, enabling version control, automated testing, and reliable deployments through CI/CD pipelines.
Grafana has an active provisioning system that uses configuration files. You can define data sources and dashboards using files that can be version controlled, making GitOps more natural.
